items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: who was Amanda Randolph, was Lillian Randolph's sister

ctx.x: Eddie Anderson, who later became Rochester, was working there with a partner, and this partner's name was Johnnie -- Johnnie, Johnnie, Johnnie, I can't think of it. Johnnie Taylor, his partner's name was Johnnie Taylor, and they had the most -- honestly, this was the funniest, the most comical act, together. They used to do acts with mops and brooms, you know. They'd be mopping the floor and going on, and all of a sudden they'd stop and tell jokes or something, and wisecracking at each other, you know. And…

Rochester was too. But this is the calibre of talent that was around. And my friend Lillian Randolph, who is still around today and doing very well. She has been in, oh God, so many marvelous pictures. She really went from the nightclub scene into the movies, you know, and to television, when television became -- in fact she was into radio first, because she did the Gildersleeve, and she was on Amos and Andy, and incidentally, the woman that was her sister, that was the mother on Amos and Andy, who was Amanda…
Yes, uh-huh. I didn't realize that was her sister.
